title: Finitely presented module tests for universal acyclicity imply K-flatness
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $E^\bullet$ an arbitrary cochain complex of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For an $A$-module $M$, write $M[0]$ for the complex equal to $M$ in degree zero and zero elsewhere, and use the direct-sum total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], specialized to ordinary modules. Suppose $\operatorname{Tot}(E^\bullet\otimes_A M[0])$ is acyclic for every finitely presented $A$-module $M$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Then $E^\bullet$ is K-flat [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. No boundedness or flatness of its individual terms is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0E8F, lemma-universally-acyclic-K-flat, specialized to commutative rings.

proof.text: We first record explicitly how filtered colimits preserve acyclicity. Let $(C_i^\bullet)$ be a diagram of acyclic module complexes indexed by a small nonempty directed set, and form its degreewise module colimit $C^\bullet$ with differential induced by the $d_{C_i}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise], a cycle $z\in C^r$ has a representative $x\in C_i^r$. The equality $dz=0$ means that the image of $d x$ is zero at some later stage $j\ge i$. Thus the image $x_j$ is a cycle in $C_j^r$, hence $x_j=d y_j$ for some $y_j\in C_j^{r-1}$. The image of $y_j$ is a primitive for $z$. Every cycle is therefore a boundary, in every integer degree; no boundedness is used.

source.place: Tag 0E8F, filtered-colimit reductions; elementary cycle proof of Tag 00DB using Tags 00D6 and 00D7

proof.text: For the rest of the proof write $T(N^\bullet)=\operatorname{Tot}(N^\bullet\otimes_A E^\bullet)$, with the direct sums and differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. This functor commutes with degreewise colimits over any small directed set. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-commutes-with-colimits] gives the comparison in each bidegree $(p,q)$. Direct sums commute with colimits: giving a map from either iterated colimit to a module $B$ is exactly giving maps $N_i^p\otimes_A E^q\to B$ compatible in $i$, one for each $p+q=r$. This proves the comparison isomorphism in total degree $r$. On a pure tensor $x\otimes e$ it sends the class to $[x]\otimes e$, so the two differential terms are sent to $[d x]\otimes e+(-1)^p[x]\otimes d e$. Thus these degreewise isomorphisms are isomorphisms of complexes, natural in the diagram.

source.place: Tag 0E8F, repeated tensor-colimit comparisons; Tag 00DD, lemma-tensor-products-commute-with-limits

proof.text: Let $M$ be any $A$-module. Apply [lem-trf-module-finitely-presented-directed-colimit] with $R=A$ to write $M=\varinjlim_i M_i$ over a small nonempty directed partially ordered set, with all $M_i$ finitely presented. The hypothesis says that $\operatorname{Tot}(E^\bullet\otimes_A M_i[0])$ is acyclic. The ordinary module interchange $m\otimes e\mapsto e\otimes m$ identifies $T(M_i[0])$ with that complex: the degree of $m$ is zero, so both differentials are $m\otimes e\mapsto m\otimes d e$. Step 2 gives $T(M[0])=\varinjlim_i T(M_i[0])$, and step 1 makes this acyclic. In particular the tensor test now holds for every module, without requiring that the modules themselves be flat.

source.place: Tag 0E8F, first paragraph, using Tag 00HA, lemma-module-colimit-fp

proof.text: We prove the stronger intermediate claim that $T(N^\bullet)$ is acyclic for every bounded complex $N^\bullet$, whether or not $N^\bullet$ is acyclic. For a complex supported only in degree $a$, write its unique module as $M$ (the notation is $M[-a]$). Its total tensor with $E$ has degree-$r$ term $M\otimes_A E^{r-a}$ and differential $(-1)^a(1\otimes d_E)$. Multiplication of a differential by the unit $(-1)^a$ changes neither its kernel nor its image. Its cohomology therefore vanishes by step 3. The zero complex has zero total tensor as well. These give the zero-term and one-term base cases for induction on the number of degrees in a supporting interval $[a,b]$.

source.place: Tag 0E8F, bounded-complex induction, base cases made explicit

proof.text: For the induction step let $N^r=0$ outside $[a,b]$, where $a<b$, and put $N_{>a}^r=N^r$ for $r>a$ and zero otherwise, with inherited differentials. The inclusion and the projection onto $N^a[-a]$ are chain maps and give $0\to N_{>a}\to N\to N^a[-a]\to0$, split in each degree. Tensoring its degree-$p$ row with $E^q$ preserves the splitting: the row is the inclusion/projection sequence for a direct sum, and the inverse direct-sum maps on tensors follow from bilinearity. Taking the direct sum over $p+q=r$ gives a split exact row in every total degree $r$. The tensor differential commutes with the inclusion and projection by the formula in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] to this short exact sequence of total complexes. Induction makes $T(N_{>a})$ acyclic, and step 4 makes $T(N^a[-a])$ acyclic. Exactness of $0=H^rT(N_{>a})\to H^rT(N)\to H^rT(N^a[-a])=0$ gives $H^rT(N)=0$. This proves the bounded-complex claim for every finite supporting interval.

source.place: Tag 0E8F, final induction using the degreewise split truncation sequence; homology.tex Tag 0117

proof.text: Now let $L^\bullet$ be bounded above, with $L^r=0$ for $r>b$. For $n\in\mathbf N$ define $B_n^r=L^r$ when $r\ge b-n$ and $B_n^r=0$ otherwise, with the inherited differentials. These are subcomplexes with chain inclusions $B_n\to B_{n+1}\to L$, and each is supported in $[b-n,b]$. For fixed $r$, the diagram of terms is eventually the constant module $L^r$ with identity transition maps. Its colimit is $L^r$: compatible maps out of the terms are uniquely determined by that eventual value. The differentials also become those of $L$, so $L=\varinjlim_{n\in\mathbf N} B_n$ degreewise. Step 5 gives acyclicity of every $T(B_n)$, step 2 identifies their colimit with $T(L)$, and step 1 proves that $T(L)$ is acyclic. No acyclicity of the brutal truncations $B_n$ was assumed.

source.place: Tag 0E8F, second reduction to bounded complexes; homology.tex Tag 0118, stupid truncations

proof.text: Finally let $F^\bullet$ be arbitrary. For $n\in\mathbf N$, define $U_n^r=F^r$ for $r<n$, $U_n^n=\ker(d_F^n)$, and $U_n^r=0$ for $r>n$. The differential into degree $n$ lands in this kernel because $d_F^n d_F^{n-1}=0$; the differential out of it is zero. Inclusions $U_n\to U_{n+1}\to F$ are chain maps, by that same kernel equation. Each $U_n$ is bounded above. At any fixed degree $r$, once $n>r$ the term and differential agree with those of $F$ and the transition maps are identities. The same eventual-value universal-property argument as in step 6 gives $F=\varinjlim_{n\in\mathbf N}U_n$ degreewise. Step 6 makes each $T(U_n)$ acyclic. Steps 2 and 1 now make $T(F)$ acyclic. This establishes the stronger conclusion for every complex $F$, including every acyclic test complex.

source.place: Tag 0E8F, canonical upper-truncation reduction; homology.tex Tag 0118, canonical cochain truncations

proof.text: For every acyclic complex $F$ of $A$-modules, step 7 proves that $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes_A E)$ is acyclic. This is precisely the defining test for K-flatness in [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Thus $E$ is K-flat, with no restriction on its bounds or on the flatness of its individual terms.
